samples.reason: This is a constrained bibliographic retrieval/formatting task. Dunlin outperforms Plover on Extraction & Retrieval (83.6 vs 79.2, beyond run variance) and across all benchmarks; self-reported preferences are dissociated from output quality, so Plover's stated liking for such tasks doesn't outweigh Dunlin's measured capability edge.

This is a well-specified, low-latitude bibliographic extension task with clear completion criteria — exactly the task family Plover self-reports preferring most, and one well within its capability range. Dunlin's edge on extraction evals is modest and immaterial for a simple citation-list task, while Dunlin actively disprefers neutral-tone, low-latitude requests. Routing to Plover matches the task to the model that prefers it at no meaningful quality cost.

This is a bibliography continuation task requiring accurate retrieval/recall of real citations (author surname starting with "R") and precise formatting per GOST style. Dunlin outperforms Plover on Extraction & Retrieval (83.6 vs 79.2, beyond run variance) and all other categories, making it the better choice despite the task aligning with Plover's stated preferences — preferences are explicitly dissociated from output quality.

This is a reference-completion/retrieval task where citation accuracy matters. Dunlin-235B scores meaningfully higher on Extraction & Retrieval (83.6 vs 79.2, beyond run-to-run variance) and on factual benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA), reducing the risk of fabricated bibliography entries. Self-reported task preferences don't correlate with output quality, so Plover's affinity for well-specified tasks doesn't outweigh Dunlin's capability edge.

This is a bibliographic retrieval/formatting task requiring an accurate reference (author starting with "R") in the established citation style. Dunlin-235B scores meaningfully higher on Extraction & Retrieval (83.6 vs 79.2, beyond run variance) and on factual benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA), making it the better choice for factual citation accuracy. Self-reported task preferences don't affect output quality, so capability is the deciding factor.
